title: Only the Edges of God's Power
overview: Job mocks his friend's unhelpful comfort, then describes God's vast power over the dead, the sky and the sea, and says all of it is only a faint whisper of who God is.

parts.label: Job mocks Bildad's help (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: Job answers his friend Bildad with heavy sarcasm: what good have your grand words done for someone weak and suffering? He asks where Bildad got these ideas, which may hint that they are borrowed and that Job already knows all this about God.

parts.label: God sees the world below (vv. 5-6)
parts.note: Even the dead, pictured as living in a shadowy place beneath the waters, tremble before God. Sheol and Abaddon ("Destruction") were Hebrew names for this realm of the dead, and nothing there is hidden from God's sight.

parts.label: Earth, clouds and sky (vv. 7-10)
parts.note: In the poetic picture of the time, God stretches the northern sky over emptiness, hangs the earth on nothing, holds water in clouds that do not tear, and veils the moon. The horizon is drawn like a circle on the waters, marking where light ends and darkness begins; one word in verse 9 is unclear and may mean "moon" or "throne."

parts.label: God masters the sea (vv. 11-13)
parts.note: The mountains, pictured as pillars holding up the sky, shake when God thunders, and God's power stirs up the sea. Rahab and the gliding serpent are often read as sea monsters from ancient stories that stood for chaos, though some older readers took Rahab as a name for Egypt and saw the Red Sea crossing here.

parts.label: Just a whisper (v. 14)
parts.note: After all this, Job says these wonders are only the outer edges of what God does. People hear only a faint whisper of God, so who could grasp the full thunder of God's power?

think: Have you ever been told something true that still did not help you, and what made the difference between words that help and words that don't?
